promptText: Linear vs Monday, which one should I choose?
rawText:
Comparing **Linear** and **Monday.com** is essentially comparing a **specialized, high-speed tool built for software teams** with a **versatile, visual platform built for all types of business teams**.

Here is a breakdown to help you decide which one fits your needs.

---

### **The Short Answer (TL;DR)**

* **Choose Linear if:** You are a software startup, product team, or engineering group that wants a lighting-fast, opinionated issue-tracking tool built specifically around software development, GitHub/GitLab workflows, and sprints.
* **Choose Monday.com if:** You need a flexible, highly visual, all-in-one project management tool to coordinate cross-functional teams (marketing, operations, HR, sales) with custom workflows, Gantt charts, and rich visual dashboards.

---

### **Key Differences at a Glance**

| Feature | **Linear** | **Monday.com** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Best For** | Software engineers, product managers | Cross-functional, business, & ops teams |
| **Core Philosophy** | Speed, simplicity, opinionated workflows | Flexibility, customization, visual control |
| **User Interface** | Dark-mode first, minimal, keyboard-driven | Bright, colorful, grid/spreadsheet-like |
| **Developer Tools** | Native deep GitHub/GitLab/Figma integration | Basic dev integrations (via third parties or apps) |
| **Workflow Style** | Sprints (Cycles), Roadmaps, Backlogs | Custom boards, Gantt, Kanban, Calendars |
| **Automation** | Smart built-in dev automations (PRs close issues) | Robust "If/Then" custom automation builder |
| **Learning Curve** | Very low for developers; high for non-tech users | Easy to start, but can get complex at scale |

---

### **1. Target Audience & Product Philosophy**

* **Linear:** Built exclusively for modern digital product teams (Engineers, Designers, Product Managers). It follows an *opinionated design*—meaning Linear dictates the best-practice framework for managing software cycles and bug tracking so you don’t waste time configuring boards.
* **Monday.com:** Built as a flexible, no-code relational database disguised as a project manager. It is *unopinionated*—you can turn a Monday board into a software backlog, a marketing calendar, an HR onboarding checklist, or a sales CRM.

### **2. Speed & User Experience (UX)**

* **Linear:** Famous for its incredible speed. It functions like a native desktop app, loads instantly, operates offline, and is almost entirely navigable via **keyboard shortcuts** (similar to VS Code). If your team hates slow Jira clicks, Linear feels like magic.
* **Monday.com:** Very visual, colorful, and spreadsheet-like. It relies heavily on drag-and-drop elements and point-and-click UI. It’s accessible for non-technical users, but large, complex boards can occasionally feel heavy or cluttered.

### **3. Software Development & Integration**

* **Linear:** Unmatched for code workflows. When a developer links a pull request (PR) in GitHub or GitLab to a Linear issue, Linear automatically updates the task status, links branch names, and auto-closes issues when code is merged.
* **Monday.com:** Has developer templates and Git integrations, but it requires manual setup and lacks the deep, native developer-centric intelligence that Linear offers.

### **4. Customization & Versatility**

* **Linear:** Purposefully limits deep customization so your workflow stays clean and standardized across your tech organization.
* **Monday.com:** Virtually endless customization. You can add dozens of custom column types (status, date, dropdown, formula, location, dropdown), build powerful visual dashboards, and create custom "If/Then" automation rules (e.g., *"When status changes to 'Approved', move item to Board B and notify marketing via Slack"*).

---

### **Pricing Comparison**

* **Linear:** Offers a generous free plan for smaller teams. Paid tiers (typically **$8 to $14 per user/month**) are straightforward and cost-effective for software teams.
* **Monday.com:** Has a limited free tier. Paid tiers generally range from **$9 to $19+ per user/month**. **Note:** Monday enforces "seat minimums" (selling seats in bundles of 3, 5, 10, etc.), which can make it pricier for small or mid-sized teams.

---

### **Final Verdict: Which Should You Choose?**

#### **Go with Linear if:**
1. You are building software, apps, or digital products.
2. Your team spends most of their time in GitHub, GitLab, Figma, and Slack.
3. You hate slow, bloated software like traditional Jira.
4. You want a tool that encourages modern Agile/Scrum best practices out of the box.

#### **Go with Monday.com if:**
1. You need a tool to manage non-technical departments (marketing, HR, legal, sales, agency client projects).
2. You want rich visual reporting, Gantt charts, and custom dashboards for executive visibility.
3. You want custom automations to bridge workflows between different teams.
4. You want a single tool that can function as a project tracker, asset manager, and lightweight CRM.
